title: TESS and Gaia DR3 data show a 76 ± 13 Jupiter-mass companion that transits the pulsating F star TIC 127799366 every 5.49 d; Gaia SB1 K agrees with 7 published RV orbits
abstract: Question: An earlier campaign study found a transit-like TESS signal at the Gaia DR3 SB1 period of the F star TIC 127799366 (Gaia DR3 5614466912454799872, G = 11.4), with no follow-up. Is it a transiting brown dwarf, and does a Gaia SB1 orbit give a reliable mass? Method: We matched 214,997 Gaia DR3 SB1-type orbits to 8,175 TOIs (ExoFOP, 2026-11-11). We compared Gaia K with the published K of all 7 transiting companions in the match that have ground RV orbits. We calculated masses (sin i = 1) and conjunction tests for 142 TOIs with a period match. For TIC 127799366 we made photometry from TESS FFI cutouts (sectors 7, 34, 61, 88), removed gamma Doradus pulsations, fitted the transit with local baselines, and measured odd/even, secondary-eclipse, phase-curve and difference-image limits. Results: Gaia K agrees with ground K (chi2 = 9.5 for 7, p = 0.22; error scale 1.17). TIC 127799366 shows 19 transits of 2.6 ppt at P = 5.493719 d, which agrees with the Gaia period (5.4943 +- 0.0031 d). With Gaia K = 6.4 +- 1.0 km/s and the FLAME host mass of 1.58 solar masses, the companion has 76 (+13/-13) MJ (P(< 78.5 MJ) = 0.58). With the FLAME density prior the radius is 1.08 +- 0.04 RJ (b = 0.88). There is no secondary eclipse (-0.07 +- 0.14 ppt) and no ellipsoidal signal (< 0.39 ppt, so q < 0.17). Difference images put the dip 3.2 +- 1.5 arcsec from the target; neighbours bright enough to cause it are 6 sigma or more away. It is a new transiting brown dwarf or very-low-mass-star candidate at the hydrogen-burning limit. Of 76 open TOIs with a Gaia orbit at the transit period, 70 have stellar-mass companions; only TOI-6218.01 (72 MJ), TOI-7584.01 (67 MJ), TOI-2533.01 and TOI-5427.01 have most-probable brown-dwarf masses, and TOI-6117.01 (86 MJ) is at the boundary. For 29 of 135 TOIs with a constrained Gaia phase, the TESS eclipse is at the other conjunction (6 are still PCs). Limitations: 7 calibration systems; Gaia K errors of 10-15 % do not separate brown dwarfs from stars near 78.5 MJ; the transit shape alone does not fix the impact parameter; pulsations add red noise; no spectra or high-resolution images. Companion masses from Gaia DR3 SB1 orbits (sin i = 1, Gaia K errors x1.17) for all TOIs with a Gaia orbit at the transit period, and for TIC 127799366 (red star). Most open TOIs (blue) have stellar companions. The shaded band is 13-78.5 MJ.

Gaia DR3 SB1 semi-amplitude K against published ground-based K for the 7 transiting companions in the TOI-Gaia match that have RV orbits. Right: normalized differences against Gaia G; chi2 = 9.5 for 7 values.

citations.reason: Reported the TESS signal of TIC 127799366 at the Gaia SB1 period; we use its QLP extract and conjunction-time code and confirm the signal with independent pixel photometry.
Gaia SB1 transit test; our mass census agrees that real transiting companions among Gaia brown-dwarf candidates are at the top of the mass range.
Flagged TOIs with Gaia RV scatter or an NSS period match; we give orbit-based masses for the period-matched TOIs and confirm that most are stellar.
Schmidt et al. 2023: Gaia SB1 solutions for three transiting low-mass secondaries; source of ground K for TOI-2533 and TOI-5427.
Grieves et al. 2021: ground RV orbits of TOI-148 and TOI-746.
Subjak et al. 2020: ground RV orbit of TOI-503.
